note: Allowlisted sources only. Excerpts are from the Team A brief and STEP guide descriptions of those pages — not a live scrape. A row without a quote from this file is dropped.

sources.title: The Star, 15 March 2026
sources.what: Nairobi county mapping of 37 flood-prone neighbourhoods
sources.excerpt: Government mapping exercise, March 2026, providing background on Nairobi’s 37 flood hotspots. The kit geocodes 24 of those 37 names. This is a name list, not a water-depth gauge.

sources.title: Kenya Climate Directory, 2024
sources.what: Diagnostic of urban flooding in Nairobi — drainage capacity and flood mechanisms
sources.excerpt: 2024 report covering drainage capacity and flood mechanisms. The STEP guide states the TIFF proxy misses corridors that flood from localized drainage-system overload rather than terrain or river proximity — Kibera, Westlands, Lavington, Kitisuru, and other generally more affluent suburbs.

sources.title: nairobi_hotspots_geocoded.csv
sources.what: 24 of 37 government-named neighbourhoods with OpenStreetMap coordinates
sources.excerpt: Ground truth for checking whether the hazard layer makes sense — not exposure data. 13 of the 37 named areas are not in this file.

sources.title: STEP_BY_STEP_GUIDE — Team A proxy check
sources.what: Kit measurement: proxy flags 12 of 24 named hotspots
sources.excerpt: The proxy correctly flagged 12 of 24 — mainly the Eastlands informal-settlement cluster along the Nairobi River (Kayole, Njiru, Kiambiu, Mwiki, Mathare, Dandora, and others). The 12 it missed flood for drainage-system overload, which this kind of proxy structurally cannot see.

sources.title: JRC / Huizinga depth–damage functions
sources.what: Published global flood depth–damage curves used as the vulnerability shape
sources.excerpt: Reference for the sigmoid depth–damage shape. Kenya parameters are an adaptation, not a local calibration. Land and foundation usually survive, so damage is capped below 100%.

sources.title: 2026 Kenya floods
sources.what: Background on the March 2026 flood event
sources.excerpt: Background on Kenya’s real March 2026 flood event. Used for context in the briefing only — not as a street-level depth.
